## Context

I keep starting evening study sessions around 8pm and drifting to midnight. My last
exam cycle went badly because I was studying tired. I am deciding between a fixed
morning block (6:30-8:30am on weekdays) and a fixed evening block (7-9pm) for the
spring term.

## Options

**Morning study block**
- 6:30-8:30am, before lectures
- Quietest room hours on campus
- Forces a fixed wake-up time
- Cuts into sleep if the previous night runs late

**Evening study block**
- 7-9pm, after dinner
- Library is busier and louder
- Easier to start after a long day
- Makes it easy to slide past midnight

## Decision

Chose the morning block. I wanted a harder start to the day and believed an early start
would be easier to keep up.

## Outcome

Reviewed 2026-08-15. Result: better.

Consistency was the real win. The morning block was easier to keep up once started,
mostly because skipping it felt like a bigger failure than skipping an evening session.
I lost about four days total across the term, most of them the morning after a late
night, and I recovered within one session each time.

Sleep was not affected the way I feared, because the fixed start forced an earlier
night. The assumption that nobody would be awake that early was wrong but harmless,
the campus is full of early-shift people by 6:30. The one thing I did not expect was
that the morning session made the rest of the day easier. I finished most problem sets
before noon, which left the afternoons free for the group project that had been eating
my evenings all last term.
